question: Does restoring the historical configured Rs range prevent PHASE6 failure when shared online gamma estimation remains enabled?

condition.pattern: PHASE6, 480 ms, PSI on, four inputs

provenance.temporary_cpp_overlay: legacy-bounds-overlay.patch; UpdateResistanceBoundsFromMembranes used max(derived, configured) for both bounds

result.cpp_refusal: unresolved amplitude overshoot at ResistanceMax; dendrite=2; tip_R=1e11; Rmax=1e11; amp_dt=-0.0484374; length=49; W3=0

comparison.fixed_saved_gamma_0_001399: A separate exact-input Release diagnostic with AutoEstimateAttenuationGamma=false reached the main C++ EOL and entered PostTune at model time about 112.246 s; its PostTune landscape result was negative and external Test classification was not run. This was a fixed-gamma ablation, not a verified replay of the historical binary.
comparison.fixed_fallback_gamma_0_05: A separate 120 s model-time capped run remained Need=1 without trainer refusal; peaks remained valid, while two inputs reached the reciprocal-range Rmax=10 GOhm.
comparison.auto_gamma_reciprocal_bounds: A separate 120 s model-time capped run remained Need=1, had invalid peaks, and ended with lengths [41,41,33,1] and sub-megaohm Rs on the first three inputs.

interpretation: Restoring the old 20 MOhm minimum avoided the sub-megaohm state seen with reciprocal bounds, and all peaks were valid at the refusal point.
The old bounds did not restore convergence: the current trainer explicitly refused at the 100 GOhm maximum with unresolved amplitude error.

The PHASE6 result is highly sensitive to online gamma policy in these controlled comparisons. The fixed 0.001399 ablation reached the synchronization and normalization gate; the auto-estimated variants did not.

This does not establish mathematical impossibility or prove a universal regression in historical runs. The reported September 8/8 result lacks an exact original executable hash, and reconstructed historical-source replays recorded elsewhere also plateaued at Rmax.

The current Classic estimator has a shared scalar gamma and updates it from observed amp/initial at length greater than one without checking SomaPeakValid or settled-length readiness. This is a concrete implementation risk to test with an isolated C++ ablation; it is not yet a complete fix proposal.
